embeds.title: 🔴 Mini Shai-Hulud Supply Chain Attack Compromises npm @antv Ecosystem Packages
embeds.description:
**Actor:** TeamPCP
Cybersecurity researchers discovered a supply chain attack campaign that compromised npm packages in the @antv ecosystem, including echarts-for-react and multiple @antv packages. Socket reports the attack matches the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign, where a compromised maintainer account (atool) was leveraged to push 639 malicious versions across 323 unique packages. The malware steals over 20 credential types including AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, GitHub, npm, SSH, Kubernetes, and database credentials, exfiltrating data to t.m-kosche[.]com:443. The campaign is assessed to be the work of TeamPCP, a financially motivated threat actor, though the source code has since been open-sourced on BreachForums, enabling copycat attacks by other threat actors.
**Sources:** thehackernews.com • 🟢 4 corroborating
**CVEs:** none • **Access:** Compromised npm maintainer account (atool)
**Incident date:** unknown • **Confidence:** claim

embeds.title: 🟢 Critical Vulnerability Exposes Industrial Robot Fleets to Hacking
embeds.description:
Universal Robots patched CVE-2026-8153, a critical OS command injection vulnerability (CVSS 9.8) in PolyScope 5 Dashboard Server affecting collaborative industrial robots. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers with network access to execute remote code on the robot's operating system. Vera Mens from Claroty discovered and reported the flaw. The patch was released in PolyScope 5.25.1. Universal Robots noted that exploitation requires the Dashboard Server to be enabled and its port to be reachable, and that UR robots are not designed for direct Internet access.
**Sources:** SecurityWeek • 🔴 1 corroborating
**CVEs:** CVE-2026-8153 • **Access:** Network access to Dashboard Server port
**Incident date:** unknown • **Confidence:** confirmed
